key_insight: Orthogonalized momentum alone can fail on nonsmooth convex objectives, but making momentum adaptive and combining it with gradient information restores reliable convergence.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-valued optimization in ML systems, MAGD offers a practical drop-in alternative to Muon when robustness on nonsmooth or nonconvex problems matters.
method: Analyze Muon under locally Lipschitz nonsmooth optimization with generalized derivatives.
Construct a failure example showing fixed-momentum Muon may miss the global optimum even with bounded iterates.
Propose MAGD: blend orthogonalized momentum and gradient using progress-based weighting, with convergence guarantees and dimension-optimal rates.
evidence_signal: The paper supports its claims with synthetic problems, image classification, and LLM pretraining experiments, alongside theoretical convergence and lower-bound results.
watch_item: Performance and guarantees rely on boundedness/regularity assumptions and on carefully tuned adaptive momentum and step-size schedules.
